title: Trump: Canadian prime minister Mark Carney is not the climate guy you thought | Seth Klein
synopsis: Canadian prime minister Mark Carney is not the climate guy you thought | Seth Klein. While Canada may be clinging to fossil fuels, much of the world is moving on Casual international observers would be forgiven for assuming Canada is in the comforting hands of a climate champ. After all, while climate policy rollbacks reign supreme in Donald Trump’s America, Canada is now led by a man who, while serving as governor of the Bank of England, delivered a celebrated 2015 speech, “ Breaking the tragedy of the horizon ”, warning the global investment community of the financial risks of climate change; who went on to serve as UN special envoy for climate action and finance ; and whose 2022 book Value(s) had much to say about the “existential threat” of climate change. A man who recently dazzled the world with his Davos speech on how middle powers can stand up to global bullies. Look, we get it. Next to the US president, Carney seems so debonair, thoughtful and calm – a lifeline of stability in a volatile new world. Seth Klein is a Canadian climate writer and activist, author of the book A Good War: Mobilizing Canada for the Climate Emergency , and former team lead of the Climate Emergency Unit . title: Trump Calls FIFA President to Overturn Balogun Red Card — First World Cup Suspension Reversal Since 1962
synopsis: President Trump personally called FIFA President Gianni Infantino to demand a review of US striker Folarin Balogun's automatic one-match red card suspension before the Round of 16 match against Belgium. FIFA's disciplinary committee then invoked an obscure Article 27 to suspend the ban for a one-year probationary period — the first time since Brazil's Garrincha in 1962 that a World Cup red card suspension was overturned. Trump took credit at the White House, saying "I'm the one that got them to do it." UEFA declared FIFA had "crossed a red line" calling it "unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable." The complaint builds on a December 2025 filing about Infantino's creation of the "FIFA Peace Prize" awarded to Trump at the World Cup draw. IOC President Kirsty Coventry confirmed the body was "watching everything play out." The complaint is backed by Norway's football federation and approximately 50 members of the European Parliament. Infantino holds IOC membership since 2020, giving the Ethics Commission jurisdiction over his conduct.
rationale: Demonstrates how Trump's corruption of sports governance triggered formal international accountability mechanisms. The IOC referral, combined with the earlier FIFA ethics complaint and UEFA condemnation, creates a multi-institutional investigation into political interference in the world's largest sporting event — all traced directly back to one phone call from the US President to his ally Infantino.

The action, branded "Unitas Mundi" (Latin for "Unity of the World"), drew attention to both the Balogun scandal and broader concerns about the intersection of authoritarian politics and international sports governance.

The symbolic use of red cards — the same instrument Trump corrupted through his Infantino call — turned FIFA's own disciplinary tool into a protest symbol against presidential overreach and immigration cruelty.

synopsis: Jared Kushner's private equity firm Affinity Partners, alongside Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and Silver Lake, completed the $55 billion acquisition of Electronic Arts — the largest-ever buyout funded by private equity. title: GAO Audit: Musk's DOGE Overstated $110B in Savings — Took Credit for Pre-Existing Cuts, Unverified Claims
synopsis: The Government Accountability Office published a devastating audit finding that Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency consistently inflated its claimed $110 billion in savings. GAO found that of 13,476 contracts DOGE claimed to terminate, 2,503 had "no termination action" taken. Of 264 leases DOGE claimed to cut, 108 were already being terminated before DOGE existed. DOGE claimed $113 million in lease savings but the actual figure was $53.5 million. A touted $1.7 billion DoD IT contract termination resulted in zero savings because no action was ever taken. The GAO recommended DOGE's website prominently warn readers about "data-quality problems." Senator Gary Peters called it a "slapdash and deceptive effort that misled the American people." The audit covered DOGE activity from Jan 20, 2025 through July 7, 2026 — three days after DOGE announced it had wound down.
rationale: The GAO audit proves what critics alleged from the start: DOGE was performance art masquerading as fiscal responsibility. Musk's operation claimed credit for savings it didn't generate, terminated contracts that weren't terminated, and published unreliable data while slashing hundreds of thousands of government jobs. The "Wall of Receipts" — DOGE's signature accountability claim — was itself unaccountable. This confirms that the real purpose was dismantling government capacity, not achieving efficiency.

title: RFK Jr Forces FDA to Deregulate Unproven Peptides Against Agency Scientists' Recommendations
synopsis: The FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee met July 23-24 to review seven peptides — BPC-157, emideltide, epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, semax and TB-500 — that Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. pushed to deregulate despite FDA scientists concluding none had sufficient evidence for safety or efficacy. FDA briefing documents revealed most peptides had never been studied in humans. Kennedy had already reclassified 12 peptides as Category 1 substances in April, overriding FDA safety determinations. The advisory committee was stacked with new members who own or work at wellness centers that sell peptides. FDA scientists found TB-500 and KPV had zero human studies. Kennedy simultaneously removed FDA warnings about dangerous autism treatments including chlorine dioxide (industrial bleach) and chelation therapy. NBC reported FDA scientists publicly disagreed with Kennedy's deregulation push.
rationale: Kennedy is using HHS to override the scientific consensus within his own agency, appointing conflicted committee members to rubber-stamp deregulation of substances with no human safety data. The pattern — removing safety warnings, stacking advisory panels with industry beneficiaries, overriding career scientists — mirrors his decades of anti-science activism now wielded with cabinet-level power. Americans are being exposed to unproven injectable substances because the HHS Secretary sells wellness ideology over evidence.

title: Trump Calls Jeanine Pirro "Choked" and "Folded Like an Umbrella" — Reflecting Pool Cover-Up Exposed
synopsis: Trump publicly humiliated his hand-picked DC US Attorney Jeanine Pirro after she dropped felony vandalism charges against ex-Olympian David Hearn for allegedly damaging the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. Pirro's 20-page court filing revealed the damage was caused by "flawed installation by the contractor" — not vandalism — and that Interior Secretary Doug Burgum's department had concealed evidence including internal National Park Service communications from June 11 showing the pool liner was defective. At a "contentious" Oval Office meeting, Pirro arrived with a banker's box of evidence and accused Burgum of covering up his department's mistakes. Trump said Pirro was "totally wrong" and he was "not happy" — despite her prosecutors proving the government itself had misled the public. Three other misdemeanor cases were also dropped. Burgum continued publicly insisting "vandals" damaged the pool even after his own staff's records proved otherwise.
rationale: Exposes the Trump administration fabricating a vandalism narrative to politicize a construction defect, then turning on its own appointee when she followed the evidence. Burgum concealed exculpatory evidence while Trump promoted a false narrative. When Pirro did her job — dropping charges against an innocent person — Trump punished her publicly. This is the justice system operating as political theater: charge first, ask questions never, punish anyone who reveals the truth.

title: FBI Agents Association Files Legal Brief Against Kash Patel's Political Purge — Bipartisan Pushback Mounts
synopsis: The FBI Agents Association filed a legal brief supporting fired agents in their lawsuit against the Trump administration, marking one of five outside filings in a single week defending agents terminated by FBI Director Kash Patel. The firings targeted employees who investigated Trump or were "perceived as being against the administration's interest." The briefs, including from former FBI and DOJ alumni, argue the firings were illegal because agents were denied due process and punished for perceived political affiliation. They state the terminations "contradict decades of expectations that the bureau's apolitical, professional career corps of agents can work on sensitive cases without putting their careers at risk." Patel has pushed out dozens of employees over the past year, including those who participated in the classified documents probe, as part of what critics call remaking the FBI "in his own image."
rationale: The FBI — America's premier law enforcement agency — is being systematically purged of anyone who followed the law by investigating a sitting president. The Agents Association filing represents the institution itself pushing back against its own director. When career federal agents need legal representation against their employer for doing their jobs, the rule of law has been fundamentally compromised. This is textbook authoritarian consolidation: punish the investigators, protect the investigated.

title: Republicans Losing Faith in Hegseth — Iran War Weapons Shortfall Triggers Trump Fury at Camp David
synopsis: Multiple Republican senators publicly declared loss of confidence in Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth as the Iran war enters its sixth month with no resolution. Senator Thom Tillis said Hegseth has "lost my confidence" citing micromanagement and "impulsive decisions not grounded in reality." Senator Susan Collins called departures of senior military officials "deeply troubling." A Marquette poll showed Hegseth at minus-22 net favorability — tied with Trump for lowest in the administration. The Washington Post reported Trump confronted Hegseth at Camp David over severe munitions shortages, saying he believed the problem "had been fixed." Hegseth reportedly blamed Deputy Secretary Stephen Feinberg. NBC reported the Pentagon held a crisis meeting on the weapons shortfall after an angry Trump call. Hegseth, Joint Chiefs Chairman Dan Caine, and Feinberg asked Congress for $67 billion in supplemental funding to replenish stockpiles.
rationale: A former Fox News host with zero senior military experience now presides over a protracted war while losing confidence from his own party. The weapons shortfall — severe enough to limit US military options against Iran — exposes the cost of appointing loyalty over competence. Hegseth fired experienced generals like Randy George, replaced them with loyalists, then found himself unable to manage the war those generals were trained to fight. This is what happens when a television personality runs the Pentagon.

title: Gabbard Refuses to Confirm Iran Was Imminent Threat — DNI Deputy Resigns in Protest Over War
synopsis: Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard declined to tell Senate lawmakers whether Iran posed an "imminent threat" to the United States, deflecting questions about whether intelligence supported the White House rationale for the US-Israel war on Iran launched February 28. Her deputy Joe Kent resigned in protest the previous day, saying Iran posed no imminent threat and the joint air campaign was unnecessary. Gabbard stated Iran's nuclear program had been "obliterated" with no rebuilding efforts — undercutting Trump's stated casus belli. When pressed by Senator Jon Ossoff, she said only the commander in chief could determine what constitutes an urgent threat. Ossoff replied: "False. You're evading a question because a candid statement would contradict the White House." Gabbard omitted language from her verbal testimony that was in her prepared written remarks about Iran not rebuilding enrichment capability.
rationale: The top intelligence official in the United States cannot or will not confirm the president's justification for war. Her own deputy resigned saying the war was unnecessary. This is the intelligence community's version of the Iraq WMD moment — except this time, the DNI is silently admitting the intelligence doesn't support the war while refusing to say so publicly. Gabbard's evasion, combined with Kent's protest resignation, constitutes the clearest evidence that the Iran war was launched on false pretenses.

title: Hegseth Creates Joint Task Force to Prosecute Pentagon Leakers, Chilling Press Freedom
synopsis: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced the creation of a joint task force with Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche to expedite identification and prosecution of those leaking information to the media. In a video posted to social media, Hegseth said the Defense Department's Office of General Counsel had been given authority "to request and receive all information, records and support across the department concerning media leak investigations." All department components and personnel would be expected to prioritize these requests. The announcement came as two journalists serving on the advisory board of Stars and Stripes had filed a federal lawsuit against Hegseth on June 3, 2026, alleging that DoD "modernization" efforts violated the military newspaper's First Amendment press freedom rights.
rationale: A dedicated task force to hunt down leakers represents a direct assault on press freedom and government transparency. Whistleblowers and sources who report misconduct within the military depend on legal protections that this initiative undermines. Combined with the Stars and Stripes lawsuit, this signals systematic suppression of independent military journalism.

title: Hegseth Budget Reveals $87.6 Billion Emergency War Supplemental Amid Exhausted Stockpiles
synopsis: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth testified before the Senate Appropriations Committee defending a historic $1.5 trillion defense budget request — a 44% increase to World War II-era levels. Simultaneously, the Trump administration requested an $87.6 billion emergency supplemental package for the Iran war as strikes expanded to Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Jordan. Senator Patty Murray highlighted that much "emergency" spending was uncorrelated to Iran operations, including "$800 million for the National Guard to patrol DC," "$1 billion for the army to patrol the southern border," and "$900 million to support the administration's illegal boat strikes in the Caribbean." Independent analyst Moody's Analytics projected total war costs at $132 billion versus Hegseth's claimed $37.5 billion.
rationale: The massive gap between officially claimed costs and independent estimates suggests deliberate deception about the financial burden of the Iran war on American taxpayers. Using emergency war funding to pad unrelated programs like domestic border patrols represents misuse of military appropriations.

title: RFK Jr Holds Up $600 Million in Global Vaccine Funding Over Debunked Thimerosal Claims
synopsis: HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. held up $600 million in congressionally appropriated funds for Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, which provides vaccines to 30 low-income countries. The funds were set to expire at end of September if unused. The obstruction centered on thimerosal, a vaccine preservative Kennedy has falsely linked to autism for decades despite extensive scientific evidence showing no causal connection. Simultaneously, Kennedy spearheaded a $40-50 million research initiative across HHS agencies to seek evidence linking vaccines to chronic disease and autism — topics already extensively studied with no causal link established. Reuters reported lawmakers demanded answers as the funding freeze threatened immunization campaigns in developing nations.
rationale: Blocking $600 million in life-saving vaccines for the world's poorest children based on debunked conspiracy theories directly endangers millions of lives. Kennedy is using the power of the U.S. government to advance personal anti-vaccine ideology over decades of established science, potentially causing preventable disease outbreaks in 30 countries.

title: Worst U.S. Measles Outbreak in 35 Years Forces RFK Jr to Urge Vaccination
synopsis: HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. — a lifelong vaccine critic — was forced to publicly urge parents to vaccinate their children against measles during a heated CNN interview as the United States experienced its worst measles outbreak in 35 years. CDC data showed more measles cases had been recorded in the prior 18 months than in the previous 25 years combined. Halfway through 2026, cases surpassed the grim milestone set just the previous year. International health officials were set to meet later in the year to determine if the U.S. had lost its measles-free status — a historic public health regression directly linked to declining vaccination rates that Kennedy's own rhetoric had fueled for decades.
rationale: The catastrophic irony of America's top health official — who spent decades undermining vaccine confidence — now pleading with parents to vaccinate represents a devastating indictment of his appointment. Children are suffering preventable disease because of the man tasked with protecting their health.

title: Tulsi Gabbard Resigns as DNI — Intelligence Leadership Vacuum During Active Iran War
synopsis: Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard's resignation took effect June 30, 2026, leaving the U.S. intelligence community without permanent leadership during an active war with Iran. While Gabbard cited her husband's cancer diagnosis, PBS News reported persistent rumblings she was prepared to split with Trump over the Iran strikes. Her departure followed National Counterterrorism Center Director Joe Kent's resignation in March, who stated he "cannot in good conscience" back the war. Trump announced Aaron Lukas as Acting DNI on Truth Social. Gabbard had overseen the intelligence community through unprecedented politicization, with her confirmation being one of the most contentious in DNI history.
rationale: Loss of the intelligence chief during wartime — combined with the earlier counterterrorism director resignation over the same war — reveals deep fractures within the national security apparatus. The leadership vacuum during active conflict with Iran creates serious national security vulnerabilities.
